title: Superpolynomial semidefinite extension complexity of perfect matching
formal:
Is the semidefinite extension complexity of the perfect-matching polytopes of complete graphs unbounded by every polynomial in the number of vertices? Precisely, is
\[
\forall B,b\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\quad
\exists n\in\mathbb N\quad
\bigl(n\ge2\ \land\ 2\mid n\ \land\
\operatorname{xc}_{\mathrm{SDP}}(P_n)>Bn^b\bigr)
\]
true, for the exact real semidefinite lifts defined below?

This is a statement about the existence of representations, with arbitrary real coefficients and no symmetry or efficient-construction requirement. The quantifiers ask whether no single polynomial bounds the entire family; they do not require a specified exponential rate or a lower bound holding at every sufficiently large even size. Integer constants express the same assertion as the inherited formulation with every pair of positive real constants \(C,c\).
definitions:
For each even integer \(n\ge2\), let \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let
\[
E_n=\{\{i,j\}:i,j\in[n],\ i<j\},
\]
and let \(K_n=([n],E_n)\) be the finite simple undirected complete graph. A perfect matching is a subset \(M\subseteq E_n\) in which every vertex belongs to exactly one edge. Its incidence vector \(\chi^M\in\mathbb R^{E_n}\) has coordinate one on edges in \(M\) and zero on all other edges. Define
\[
P_n=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\text{ is a perfect matching of }K_n\}.
\]
The convex hull of a finite set consists of all weighted sums of its elements with nonnegative real weights summing to one. Thus \(P_n\) includes exactly those convex combinations, with one coordinate for each of the \(\binom n2\) edges.

For a positive integer \(r\), let
\[
\mathbb S^r=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}:Y^{\mathsf T}=Y\},
\qquad
\mathbb S^r_+=\{Y\in\mathbb S^r:\forall z\in\mathbb R^r,\ z^{\mathsf T}Yz\ge0\}.
\]
An affine subspace of \(\mathbb S^r\) is a translate of a real linear subspace. An affine map into \(\mathbb R^{E_n}\) has the form \(\pi(Y)=A(Y)+a\), with \(A\) real linear and \(a\in\mathbb R^{E_n}\). A size-\(r\) semidefinite lift of \(P_n\) is a pair \((L,\pi)\), where \(L\subseteq\mathbb S^r\) is an affine subspace and \(\pi:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^{E_n}\) is affine, satisfying the exact equality
\[
P_n=\pi(L\cap\mathbb S^r_+).
\]
The quantity \(\operatorname{xc}_{\mathrm{SDP}}(P_n)\) is the least positive integer \(r\) admitting such a pair. Every finite polytope has a finite such representation, so this minimum exists. Restricting sizes to positive integers also fixes the convention for the singleton \(P_2\).

Size means the order of this single positive semidefinite matrix, not the number of scalar entries or inequalities. If several positive semidefinite blocks are used, their block-diagonal combination counts their total order. Coefficients of \(L\) and \(\pi\) may be arbitrary real numbers. No bit-length bound, computability condition, uniform algorithm producing the representations, or efficient numerical procedure is imposed. The lifted feasible set need not be bounded or strictly feasible. No invariance under permutations of graph vertices or matrix coordinates is required. The condition \(Y^{\mathsf T}=Y\) is ordinary matrix symmetry and does not impose such an invariance requirement. Approximate outer representations do not meet the exact equality.

The inherited card uses affine projection maps. The cited survey defines lifts using linear projection maps; these conventions differ by at most one in matrix order and hence give the same polynomial-boundedness question. The original thesis asks about the polytope of all matchings, including nonperfect ones. Its family has polynomial-size exact semidefinite lifts if and only if the complete-graph perfect-matching family does, so the retained target is a polynomially equivalent formulation of the source question, not a claim that those polytopes are identical.

context_blocks.text: Perfect matching admits polynomial-time optimization, while its exact linear extension complexity is exponential.

The source asks whether positive semidefinite lifts can give polynomial-size representations of the matching polytope, a question equivalent at the family level to the retained perfect-matching version.
The benchmark allows all exact real semidefinite lifts, including representations with no symmetry or efficient construction.
Known exponential bounds for coordinate-symmetric matching formulations and general semidefinite bounds for other polytopes do not establish the unrestricted matching claim.
The later survey explicitly retains the matching question, and the bounded subsequent review found no theorem settling the precise family and model here.

why: Perfect matching is a canonical problem with efficient optimization algorithms and strong combinatorial structure. Deciding whether it nevertheless lacks polynomial-size exact semidefinite representations would clarify the limits of a major convex-optimization model beyond the established limits of linear programming. A polynomial-size family would instead demonstrate a substantial representational advantage over linear lifts for this central tractable polytope.
answer_criterion:
Provide a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the stated proposition or its full logical negation, for exactly the objects and size convention above.

A positive answer must prove that for every \(B,b\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) there is an even \(n\ge2\) for which no exact semidefinite lift has matrix order at most \(Bn^b\). This includes all real affine slices and affine projection maps, without imposing symmetry, uniformity, strict feasibility or coefficient restrictions.

A negative answer must prove
\[
\exists B,b\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\quad
\forall n\ge2\text{ with }2\mid n\quad
\exists r\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \exists L\subseteq\mathbb S^r\ \exists\pi:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb R^{E_n}\quad
\bigl(r\le Bn^b\ \land\ L\text{ is affine}\ \land\pi\text{ is affine}\
\land\ P_n=\pi(L\cap\mathbb S^r_+)\bigr).
\]
The polynomial is common to all sizes, while the representations may depend arbitrarily on \(n\); an efficient construction algorithm is not additionally required.

A lower bound for linear lifts, coordinate-symmetric semidefinite formulations, a fixed relaxation hierarchy, or a restricted coefficient field is insufficient by itself. An approximation result or an efficient matching algorithm is not an exact semidefinite representation. Conditional results must also establish any extra hypothesis needed for the unconditional target. This is an asymptotic representation-existence proposition, so no additive numerical tolerance replaces its quantified bounds.

progress.text: Rothvoß proves exponential linear extension complexity for the perfect-matching polytope of complete graphs; the restriction to linear lifts is essential when comparing this theorem with the present question.

The inspected arXiv revision of Braun and coauthors proves exponential lower bounds for coordinate-symmetric semidefinite formulations of perfect matching, including the exact case. Coordinate symmetry restricts the group action to simultaneous permutations of matrix rows and columns; the present target imposes no such restriction.
Sinha poses polynomial-size positive semidefinite extended formulations for the matching polytope as Open Question 8.4.

The SIAM Review survey explicitly lists high semidefinite extension complexity of matching polytopes as open, distinguishing it from known linear bounds and semidefinite bounds for cut and traveling-salesman polytopes.

Checked exact versus approximate representations, linear versus semidefinite size, coordinate symmetry, the full polynomial quantifiers and subsequent primary-source scopes. The bounded review found no matching resolution; this status is not an exhaustive literature certificate.

sentences: The perfect-matching polytope is the convex hull of the incidence vectors of perfect matchings in a complete graph of even order.
A semidefinite lift represents that polytope exactly as an affine image of an affine slice of a real positive semidefinite cone.
The question asks whether the required matrix order is unbounded by every polynomial in the number of graph vertices, allowing arbitrary real coefficients and separate representations at each size.
Exponential bounds for linear lifts and coordinate-symmetric semidefinite formulations leave this unrestricted representation question unresolved in the checked sources.
A complete Lean proof must establish the full lower-bound assertion or prove that one polynomial bounds exact semidefinite lifts for the entire family.

Downloaded and read actual matching-sdp-sinha2018.pdf/.txt, 181 physical pages. Open Question8.4 is printed158/PDF169. Section6.3.5 printed110–111 explicitly declines to define SDP lifts formally, correcting inherited attribution. Its PMAT(n) includes all matchings. This mathematical scope was checked independently by a second agent.

Root and independent reviewer checked Rothvoss1311.2369v4 PDF3: PM_n is a face of MATCH_n, obtained by sum_e x_e=n/2. MATCH_n is a coordinate projection of PM_2n onto edges in the first n vertices: every such perfect matching restricts to a matching, and every matching extends by using the second n vertices for uncovered vertices and then pairing those left over. Face intersections and projections preserve SDP lifts without increasing matrix order. Hence polynomial boundedness of either family is equivalent, with at most doubling n. This audit argument explains source fidelity; it is not a public suggested solution to the open problem.

Read actual matching-sdp-survey2022.pdf/.txt, latest arXiv v2 submitted19Nov2021, and verified SIAMReview64(4)866–918(2022) DOI10.1137/20M1324417 metadata. Definition1.4 PDF6 defines affine L and linear pi. For affine pi(X)=A(X)+a, enlarge X to blockdiag(X,1); the new map A(X)+a times the last diagonal coordinate is linear. Conversely every linear projection is affine. Thus sizes differ at most1 and polynomial boundedness agrees. No exact equality of the numerical minima under the two conventions is claimed.

Read LP separation and other-cone context to avoid confusing copositive/completely-positive cones with real PSD cones. Integer B,b>=1 and even n>=2 preserve inherited forall-positive-real-C,c/no-polynomial-bound assertion by rounding constants upward.
